It drops the manifest-level verdict_ids roster and instead binds verdict_id and candidate_digest onto each criterionDisposition row, so a row's evidence is traceable to the exact verdict and the exact candidate digest that produced it, matching evidence_policy.candidate_binding: current_digest at the row level. /v1 stays committed, unedited, and locked to its own recorded shape digest by tests/contracts/evidence/test_evidence_manifest.py::TestSchemaVersioningDiscipline; this file is that same test's lock target for schema.const ctower.evidence-manifest/v2. title/description/$comment stay free to edit.
contracts/evidence/evidence-manifest-v2..description: Development-only CP-1 typed evidence denominator. The criterion denominator is what this increment owes: the criteria frozen by the authored gate policies plus every acceptance criterion the canonical specification declares, and each one carries exactly one typed disposition, its own verdict id, and its own candidate-digest binding. The generated traceability index is a coverage map, not a source of obligations, and is not read. The deferred denominator is the deferred suites of the expected-suite registry; capability components are not a denominator source, so an exercised capability is never forced to declare itself unexercised. Gate-policy criterion keys, acceptance-criterion codes and suite ids each keep their own namespace.

criteria.$comment: uniqueItems refuses an identical repeated row. JSON Schema 2020-12 cannot express uniqueness by key, so a repeated criterion carrying a different payload is refused by name at the criterion chokepoint in tests/contracts/evidence.

deferred_suites.$comment: minItems refuses an empty deferred roster while the expected-suite registry still defers a suite; uniqueItems refuses an identical repeated row. A repeated suite id carrying a different payload is refused by name at the deferred-suite chokepoint in tests/contracts/evidence.

entry_state.description: The leased entry, in the field names the kernel's own pool observations already use: one vocabulary across the worker plane and the record tier, so a lease and a `poolObservationEntry` never have to be translated into each other. Three orthogonal axes plus registration. AUTH is not QUOTA is not REACH: collapsing them is what prescribes a re-mint against a credential that was never broken. The names here are exactly the projection allowlist a reader may take off an engine record — the fields beside them are the credential itself.

entry_label.description: A display attribute with no authority. Two identically-named labels have hidden two different accounts.

secret_fingerprint.description: A reference, never a value. This is the only credential-shaped field the lease carries.

subscription_identity.description: The entry's own decoded identity claim. Entries are keyed by identity and never by label.

contracts/runner/credential-lease.schema.description: What `acquire` returns: which pool entry an attempt rides, as a reference. Credentials are read at spawn, so a lease is part of an attempt's immutable pinned composition and a rotation reaches a running lane only through a respawn. There is no field a credential value can occupy.
contracts/runner/credential-lease.schema.title: CredentialLease

contracts/runner/harness-capability.sche.description: A capability is declared data, never a runtime discovery. The closed list is the whole vocabulary a binding may claim; an undeclared capability is unsupported by name rather than attempted.
contracts/runner/harness-capability.sche.title: HarnessCapability

kind.description: What proves the brief was accepted. Delivery is not acknowledgement.

submit_separately.description: True where the composer needs a submit keystroke distinct from the delivery itself.

layers.description: Declared role per layer. Never both: a native layer plus ctower's own over one credential set is a race over single-use refresh chains, not redundancy.

proves.description: `serving` is truth; `request` is recorded as a conflict and never as serving truth.

cache_invalidation_hook.description: Named hook that must complete before any entry state observed after a rotation is believed.

model_ref.description: The model the seats actually run. A probe aimed elsewhere reports unknown for the seats' rung.

survey.description: The answered capability survey. An unanswered survey leaves the per-layer role undecidable, which is a refusal rather than a gap.

contracts/runner/harness-spec.schema.jso.description: One revision-pinned harness binding, declared as data. Parsed without executing package code: an adapter that cannot declare a capability does not discover it at runtime.

context_window_percent.description: Declared saturation threshold as a percentage of this binding's own window. The percentage is the portable signal; an absolute token count proves nothing across window sizes.

key.description: The observed harness value, carried byte-for-byte and never normalized.

liveness_sources.description: Declared evidence sources. A fact with no declared source returns unknown by name, never a guess.

status.description: Registration status. `revoked` is a refusal at dispatch, never a fallback to a generic process.

contracts/runner/harness-spec.schema.jso.title: HarnessSpec
